I played the original version of Metro 2033 on PC; I remember getting it free from a giveaway by Humble Bundle, so I added it to my Library, and upon building my PC earlier this year, it was one of the first games I played to test out my hardware.

Metro 2033 is a first person shooter, based on the novel of the same name, which I admit I haven't personally read. Metro 2033's setting is post-apocalyptic Russia, due to a nuclear attack. Moscow lies in ruin, and the citizens have retreated to the Metro system to take shelter from the hell on earth. You play as Artyom, who encounters many different enemies throughout his travels, both below ground in the Metro, and above ground in what's left of the city. Each has their own problems - the Metro sees various factions fighting, and the surface sees toxic air requiring a gas mask for navigation, along with the constant need of finding filters before your time runs out.

As a shooter, it's very solid. Each weapon feels fairly different, which is nice, and the main weapons types each use a different type of ammunition. Ammo plays a significant role in Metro 2033, as there are 2 key types. 'Military grade' rounds offer a higher damage, but they're primary use is as currency, due to their scarcity - these are mainly sourced from scavenging dead bodies of previous adventurers, your freshly slain enemies, and just what's been dropped at one time or another. Alternatively, however, there are 'dirty rounds' (if I remember the name right), which are cheap and what will ultimately be your main source of bullets, but deal a lower damage compared to military grade ammo. My only gripe with it as a currency, is that you could pretty much get through the entire game without buying, as you'll just find what you need from your foes. There are a couple points where you'll buy something with military grade rounds, but 9/10 purchases will be dirty bullets, and even those are easily scavenged. It's not a bad system at all, but you probably won't fear running out.

The story, I must mention, is very, very good. Despite being a first person shooter, the plot is very well written, with some good twists and turns to keep you on edge. I'd even go as far to say it's fairly 'realistic', as far as post apocalyptic Russia could ever be anyway. I guess, it's not that hard to see just how the game's world got to where it is - and the oppressive atmosphere is enough motivation to keep charging through to see just where you end up. The ending is also very well done, as it provides full closure in terms of plot, but like the original Mass Effect and a handful of other games, it does well to leave you wanting more. The game even has a few neat mechanics at play, although I'll leave them out here.

The original version of Metro 2033, however, is hard to get a hold of. I think Humble Bundle has given away the original Metro 2033 multiple times, so it may help to keep an eye out there, or alternatively purchase the 'Redux' version from Steam, which features new mechanics implemented from it's sequel, Metro Last Light, along with other polish and fixes. Physically however, it may be easier to source a retail copy from somewhere like Amazon. The original is only available on Xbox 360, whereas PS4 and Xbox One players will need to pick up the 'Metro Redux' double pack, featuring both of the remastered versions.

Personally, I didn't encounter any issues. I believe I had it crash a couple times when first opening up, but hitting Play again threw me into the game fine. Nothing play-stopping. However, I have heard of other people encountering issues, as is the nature with any PC game.

8/10: A harrowing vibe keeps you on edge, along with the naturally oppressive atmosphere Metro 2033 provides. The gameplay is solid, the graphics are very good, and the plot will leave you wanting to pick up it's sequel, which I also recommend. Metro is an experience like no other, and offers a neat balance between horror, action, and stealth.
